- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +0.8 to -0.5 in 3–5 days), model exhibits lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction within 2–4 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if price has moved >3% from 10-day average, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply 1–2% downward correction for days 1–7.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.5 → -0.3 → +0.2), model fails to adjust; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast.
